profiles.description: Owns the carrier's financial crime and BSA/AML control framework, drafting the risk-based AML compliance policy, designating the AML compliance officer accountabilities, and defining AML key risk indicators and committee reporting thresholds. Runs the sanctions program end to end: authoring the sanctions screening policy, configuring OFAC/UN/EU list updates into the screening engine, calibrating fuzzy name-matching thresholds, screening beneficiaries at payment execution, and performing annual reviews of list coverage and control gaps. Also calibrates transaction monitoring rules and scenario thresholds and validates SAR completeness before AML officer approval, supported by financial crime intelligence, typology analysis, and financial crime committee reporting. Leads AML work in the Finance Investments and Risk Compliance Audit value streams, matching the designated-officer role that regulators expect to coordinate day-to-day AML compliance and brief senior management.

profiles.notes: Sources describe the designated BSA/AML officer as director-level with authority to report to the C-suite; 'Manager' is the closest level in the allowed set. Packet ownership (21 of 35 tasks) is consistent with the FFIEC-style designated-officer model.

profiles.description: Leads cloud financial management for the carrier's Technology & Engineering organization, owning cloud cost visibility and reporting: reconciling cloud spend to monthly provider invoices, distributing cloud cost summaries to stakeholders, and producing the rolling cloud spend forecast. Defines the mandatory cost-allocation tag taxonomy and generates per-team showback statements, tying cloud cost back to budgets and unit economics for policies, claims, and transactions. Participates in adjacent finance and procurement work, including risk-adjusted return calculations by line of business, TCO/savings analysis in sourcing, and contract spend-to-commitment reconciliation. The scope maps directly onto the FinOps Foundation's invoicing/chargeback, allocation, and forecasting capabilities, sitting at the intersection of finance and engineering.

profiles.description: Owns the carrier's financial planning, forecasting, and management reporting cycles across annual budget development, rolling forecast/reforecast, and strategic long-range planning — building the 5-year premium and loss-ratio projection model, translating corporate strategy into financial targets by business line, and assembling the strategic plan narrative and exhibits. Prepares the operations performance pack for leadership review and drives workforce capacity planning by forecasting incoming work volumes and translating them into required FTE capacity. Provides decision support into HR compensation planning (merit budget pools, incentive accrual reconciliation) and PMO funding decisions via business cases and benefit estimates. Also covers cost allocation and transfer pricing, capital expenditure governance, and variance analysis, consistent with the FP&A manager's standard remit of budgets, forecasts, and executive reporting.

profiles.description: The carrier's senior-most legal officer, leading the Legal Corporate Governance value stream: approving dispositive and substantive motion strategy in litigation, obtaining settlement authority sign-off, and advising on employment claims and response strategy. Owns regulatory-facing legal work including approving final insurance department examination dispositions, signing off and submitting corporate governance annual disclosure filings, and defining minimum governance standards for each legal entity tier. Sets annual legislative priorities and advocacy positions and approves trade association and coalition memberships. Also compiles SOX testing results for management certification, reflecting the modern GC's expanded governance and controls remit as advisor to the board and executive team.

profiles.description: Manages the carrier's public policy and government relations agenda: tracking introduced bills across target state legislatures and Congress, briefing affected business owners on pending legislative changes, and publishing horizon-scanning digests of upcoming regulatory developments. Runs the lobbying and advocacy program — engaging external lobbyists, defining advocacy scopes of work, and conducting legislator outreach on priority positions — alongside political contributions compliance and coalition/stakeholder engagement. Maintains regulatory relationships with state departments of insurance, documenting outcomes and commitments from DOI engagements. This mirrors the standard state government affairs remit of legislative tracking, lobbyist management, and policy position development coordinated with legal and regulatory teams.

profiles.description: Leads the broker channel for the carrier, setting broker distribution strategy, channel growth priorities, and broker relationship governance per the packet's responsibilities. Manages channel economics, production quality, and distribution investment priorities, and reviews broker performance, production mix, pipeline quality, and service issues. Coordinates distribution plans with underwriting, product, marketing, and operations, and approves channel actions, incentive changes, and broker segmentation plans. Industry sources describe the same remit for senior broker-channel leaders: choosing and managing external producer relationships, appointments, tiered commission structures, and channel strategy trade-offs.

profiles.description: Leads the carrier's capital management function: assessing the capital position against risk appetite, projecting capital needs and running the capital plan, and allocating capital across business units per the packet's responsibilities. Executes capital actions such as dividends and issuance and monitors ongoing capital utilization. The role operates against the regulatory backdrop of NAIC risk-based capital, where insurers must continuously hold and monitor capital in proportion to risk and manage adequacy ratios ahead of intervention thresholds. Industry role descriptions confirm the remit spans capital projection modeling, capital-injection support and allocation, regulatory capital compliance, and executive-level reporting on capital results.

profiles.description: Leads the enterprise compliance framework for the carrier across the Risk Compliance Audit and Risk, Compliance & Regulatory Management value streams, owning policy and procedure governance — publishing approved policies, triggering attestation assignments, and distributing and capturing control-owner attestations. Sets compliance priorities, the monitoring approach, and issue escalation across business functions, participating in risk-based compliance testing plans, remediation action closure, and mapping regulatory obligations to testable control statements. Presents compliance status to the compliance committee and participates in AML and sanctions programme governance, including AML officer designation and the sanctions screening policy. This matches the chief-compliance-officer profile of an executive-level leader who builds and maintains the compliance framework, faces regulators, and reports to governance committees.

profiles.description: Sets the carrier's overall distribution strategy across channels, leading the Sales Distribution Marketing and Distribution & Channel Management value streams: securing executive sign-off on the channel and segment strategy, allocating the distribution budget across channels and quarters, and signing off the channel investment plan with distribution leadership. Owns producer compensation governance, reviewing and approving the commission governance policy and controls, and participates in commission schedule activation and contingent compensation payment release. Coordinates broker strategy with underwriting leadership and product teams and reviews production, hit ratio, and relationship performance trends. This matches the industry pattern where distribution leadership harmonizes multi-channel strategy, channel economics, and tiered producer compensation with auditable governance.

profiles.description: Directs day-to-day IT delivery, service management, and operational performance for the carrier's Technology & Engineering division, leading the Technology Engineering and Technology Strategy, Architecture & Delivery value streams. Owns IT change governance: obtaining CAB pre-authorization for new standard change types, convening the eCAB for expedited emergency change authorization, and conducting post-emergency reviews. Approves API standards exceptions for legacy consumers, authors and ratifies the cloud cost governance (FinOps) policy, and oversees secret/certificate/credential management. Sources describe the same profile — a senior leader over infrastructure, service delivery, governance and policy, budgets, and vendor management, positioned below the CIO/CTO but above IT managers.

profiles.description: Leads pricing strategy, rate adequacy, and pricing governance for the carrier's Actuarial division across the Actuarial, Underwriting, and Actuarial Pricing, Reserving & Capital Modeling value streams. Owns assumption governance and change management — rolling approved assumptions into production models with an audit trail — and the rate filing lifecycle, drafting the actuarial memorandum and certification and approving the final rate filing for submission. Manages quote expiry and re-pricing, participates in P&C loss cost and trend studies, recommends rate and assumption changes to the pricing committee, and helps present the actuarial report to the board committee. The remit tracks ASOP 54's requirements for assumption setting, oversight, and documented governance and controls in pricing, and the senior pricing actuary's end-to-end accountability for product pricing.

profiles.description: Sets the carrier's enterprise reinsurance strategy and aligns protection purchases to risk appetite and capital objectives, leading the Reinsurance and Reinsurance & Retrocession Management value streams. Approves the annual reinsurance strategy and appetite, signs off the reinsurance ledger close result, authorizes assumed lines above delegated authority, and participates in program structuring (treaty vs facultative), net retention setting, renewal planning, and reinsurance budgeting. Coordinates placements with brokers, underwriting, actuarial, finance, and risk, and reviews ceded program performance, counterparty quality, and recoverables — the classic ceded-reinsurance leadership scope of retentions, treaty terms, renewals, and capital relief. Also owns committee reporting on the share repurchase / capital return program in the Finance Investments value stream.

profiles.description: Acts as the strategic HR counterpart to business-unit leaders, owning capability and workforce demand planning: collecting hiring forecasts and attrition assumptions, translating skill gaps into build/buy/borrow sourcing recommendations, and publishing the workforce demand plan for leadership endorsement. Owns organization design and job architecture work — drafting target-state org design options, defining the job family taxonomy, and writing leveled job profiles — plus succession planning for critical and single-point-of-failure roles and mapping affected employees through organizational change and workforce transitions. Extends into the hiring lifecycle, calculating offer packages against compensation bands. With 116 linked tasks across 25 deliverables, this is the broadest HR role in the packet, consistent with sources describing HRBPs as senior advisors on workforce planning, org design, succession, and change rather than HR administrators.

Supports HR policy governance by publishing approved policies, assigning mandatory acknowledgments, and monitoring completion and exceptions. Also tracks actuarial continuing-education and qualification credits in support of the Actuarial value stream, alongside background check, licensing, and compliance training tracking. This matches the standard HR coordinator profile — an entry-to-mid-level role processing HRIS transactions, coordinating onboarding logistics and scheduling, and maintaining accurate employee and organizational records.

profiles.description: Administers identity and access management across the carrier's business systems from the Cybersecurity & IAM division: provisioning joiner identities from the HR authoritative feed, provisioning system access, email, and security badges for start dates, and provisioning/deprovisioning HR system access by role. Owns provisioning of marketing automation user roles and permissions as part of martech stack administration, and supports HRIS integration monitoring, cybersecurity policy exception tracking, and the security awareness program (curriculum design, mandatory training assignment, phishing simulations). Per the packet responsibilities, the role also runs quarterly access certification campaigns, maintains role-based access models and segregation-of-duties rule sets, remediates orphaned and privileged account exceptions, and supplies access evidence for SOX and regulatory audits.
